itemListElement.name: How Much Should a Small Business Website Cost? What You Are Actually Paying For

mainEntity.name: How much does a small business website cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single price. Cost depends on the number of pages, custom design versus a template, who writes the content, the features you need, the number of languages and who builds it. Compare quotes by what they include and by what you will pay after launch, not by the headline number alone.

mainEntity.name: Why are website quotes so different from each other?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the scope behind each quote is usually different. One may include writing, photos and search setup, another may not. Ask each builder to list exactly what is included before comparing prices.

mainEntity.name: What ongoing costs should I expect after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for your domain renewal, hosting, maintenance and security updates, small content changes and any paid tools or plugins. Ask each builder which of these are included and which are billed separately.

mainEntity.name: Should I build my website myself or hire someone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your time, your skills and how much the site matters to winning customers. A website builder costs less in cash and more in your own hours. Hiring a professional costs more in cash and saves you time and design risk.

mainEntity.name: Do I own my website and domain?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should. Register the domain in your own name and keep control of your hosting account, content and design files. Ask any builder to confirm this in writing.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a website is worth the money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start from what a customer is worth to you. Divide the total cost by your profit per job to see how many extra jobs the site needs to bring in to pay for itself, then judge whether that is realistic for your market.

mainEntity.name: Does my website need to be in more than one language?

acceptedAnswer.text: If part of your customer base searches and buys in Spanish or Portuguese, a version written for that audience can help. Each language needs its own pages, so it adds to the cost. Decide based on who your customers actually are.
